CRIMINAL CASE No. 45655 of 2024  MURARI JATAV  Versus
THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH

Appearance:
 Shri Dhirendra Singh Niranjan, Advocate for the applic  Shri K.K. Prajapati, Public Prosecutor for the respond  ORDER

This is first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. (S.483 of BNSS ) for grant of bail relating to Crime No. 258 of 2023 registered at Police Station Lahar, District Bhind (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 366, 376D, 376(2)(n) and 506 Part II of the IPC.
Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated.
He is in custody since 30/5/2024.

The entire prosecution story is highly improbable and suspicious in the light of the fact that prosecutrix is a major married woman and allegedly the applicant/accused forcibly took her with him to Gwalior and Jabalpur through public transport along with her children.
However, there is no evidence that she tried to escape or raise alarm.
Further submission is that the prosecutrix lived with the applicant/accused in Jabalpur for almost 20-25 days with her children.
Under these circumstances, not lodging any report or NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:19399 2 MCRC-45655-2024 making any complaint to anyone is improbable.
Further submission is that the evidence of prosecutrix as PW1 and her husband as PW2 have already been recorded.
The court-statement of prosecutrix clearly indicates that it is a case of consent.

Further submission is that since the prosecutrix has already been examined, therefore,
question of influencing her does not arise.
After conclusion of investigation, charge-sheet has already been filed, therefore, custodial interrogation is not required anymore.

sentences.text: 1 permanent resident of Village Karhiya, P.S. Karhiya, District Gwalior (M.P.) and there is no possibility of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
He shall abide by all the terms and conditions as may be imposed by this Court.
Hence, he prays for grant of bail to the applicant.
Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor for respondent/State opposed the bail application and prayed for dismissal of present bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal court.

In case offence of same nature is repeated, this bail order shall automatically stand cancelled;
v) The applicant will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial; and vi) The applicant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
Learned State counsel is directed to send an e-copy of this order to the Station House Officer of the concerned Police Station for information and necessary action.
E- copy of this order be sent to the trial Court concerned for compliance, if possible, by the office of this Court.
Certified copy as per rules.

(SUNITA YADAV) JUDGE (and)
